body:

• Added "Always deliver" to the prompt for held messages from other sessions

• Added a warning in VS Code and Desktop's Code tab when part of a session couldn't be saved, saying how to save it with /compact

• Fixed claude auth login reporting Login successful. when a claude.ai login could not be saved: it now exits 1 and says what to check, such as a leftover lock file or a full disk
• Fixed Read, @-mentions and compaction hanging on a named pipe that nothing writes to, such as a .env mounted by a locked secrets manager; the read now fails after 20 seconds
• Fixed turns ending in…
headline: MCP server skills (beta) and PreSkillShellCommand hook
takeaway: You can now invoke skills from MCP servers via server:skill in the / menu and block inline shell commands in skills using PreSkillShellCommand.

title: Codex CLI 0.172.0

New Features:
• Follow thread links from search results and transcripts to open saved conversations and nested agents in the terminal. (#62332)
• Press Tab to complete arguments for supported slash commands. For example, /mcp lo completes to /mcp login. (#62343)

• Codex reports provider errors as soon as they arrive in a response stream and identifies which API spend limit was reached. (#62329, #62356)
• Interrupting a parent turn preserves queued replies from child agents for the next turn. (#62348)
• Use PageUp and PageDown to read and submit answer choices that are taller than the terminal’s answer area. (#62209)

Documentation:
• The bundled openai-docs skill now…

takeaway: Open saved conversations from search, Tab-complete slash commands like /mcp login, lazy-start cached MCP servers, and select Amazon Bedrock Runtime during setup.

title: Open a session side by side
body: Option/Alt+click a session link to open it in a split pane.

takeaway: Option/Alt+click any session link to open it in a split pane, making it easier to compare or monitor multiple sessions at once.

title: Session search moves to the command palette

headline: Devin moves session search to the Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette
takeaway: Search sessions using Cmd/Ctrl+K instead of the removed inline search in the Sessions sidebar.

title: Code scan cancellations in audit logs
body: Audit logs record who cancelled a code scan, from the web app or the v3 API.
headline: Audit logs now record who cancelled Devin code scans
takeaway: Track who cancelled a code scan—whether from the web app or the v3 API—directly in your audit logs.

title: Warning before deleting secrets used by Preflight checks
body: Before you delete an org secret, the Secrets page lists the automations whose Preflight checks use it.
headline: Devin warns before deleting secrets used by Preflight checks
takeaway: Before deleting an org secret, the Secrets page lists any automations whose Preflight checks depend on it.

title: Offer marketplace plugins to members
body: Admins can mark a marketplace plugin as Offered to members instead of Required.
headline: Admins can mark Devin marketplace plugins as Offered
takeaway: Instead of making a marketplace plugin Required, admins can now mark it as Offered to members.

title: Allow an MCP tool for the whole session
body: MCP tool approval cards add Allow for this session.
headline: Allow an MCP tool for the entire Devin session
takeaway: MCP tool approval cards now include an Allow for this session option so you don't have to re-approve repeated calls.

title: API-key MCP headers bound to secrets
body: Blank headers on API-key marketplace MCP servers are bound to secrets, and unused secrets are flagged.
headline: API-key marketplace MCP headers now bind to secrets
takeaway: Blank headers on API-key marketplace MCP servers automatically bind to secrets, and unused secrets are flagged.

title: Custom MCP servers default to Automatic authentication
body: New custom MCP servers start with Automatic authentication selected.
headline: Custom MCP servers now default to Automatic authentication
takeaway: When adding a new custom MCP server in Devin, Automatic authentication is pre-selected to speed up setup.

title: Run automations from the right-click menu
body: Right-click a row on the Automations list for Run now, Open in new tab and Copy link.
headline: Right-click menu added to Automations list
takeaway: You can now right-click any automation row to quickly run it, open it in a new tab, or copy its link.

title: Claude Code 2.1.331
body:
What's changed:
• Added Code Mode support in terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS
• Added oidc.groups_jsonpath to the Claude apps gateway, to read groups from the matching entries of a list of objects with a small subset of JSONPath (RFC 9535)
• Added an API connectivity section to claude doctor that reports whether the API can be reached, with the HTTP status or the error, or says why it wasn't tested
• Added a notice when tap-mode voice dictation stops by itself, after 15 seconds without recognized speech or at its 2-minute limit
• Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_RESPONSE_COMPRESSION to ask for uncompressed model responses behind a proxy that cuts compressed ones off; not advised yet for self-hosted runners or Remote Control
• Added CLAUDE_GATEWAY_IDP_CONNECT_BY_HOSTNAME=1 for Claude apps gateways: with oidc.use_proxy: true, sign-in requests hand the proxy an https IdP's hostname even with NO_PROXY set
• Added gen_ai.usage., gen_ai.response.model and gen_ai.operation.name to claude_code.llm_request trace spans; gen_ai.usage.input_tokens includes prompt cache tokens
• Added optionalDependencies to plugin manifests: plugins that install with the plugin listing them and can be disabled or uninstalled on their own
• Fixed MCP tool calls hanging for up to 30 minutes on some malformed replies from a local or WebSocket server
• Fixed PushNotification telling a headless run, such as a scheduled one, that the…
headline: Code Mode in terminal sessions on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry
takeaway: Terminal sessions now support Code Mode on Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry, and AWS, plus claude doctor checks API connectivity.

title: SCM access mismatch checker
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. Admins get a report of repos where access in Devin is different from access in GitHub or GitLab. Admins can also turn on repo sync, which adds the repos you have in GitHub or GitLab to your repo picker. Repos your org already added stay.
headline: SCM access mismatch checker and repo sync
takeaway: Enterprise admins can spot GitHub/GitLab vs. Devin repo access mismatches and sync repos to the picker (off by default).

title: Shareable environments available
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. All users by default will be able to create an environment once and use it in any org. Admins will be able to remove this permission from the default member role. You only see environments whose repos you have access to. Existing environments are unchanged.
headline: Shareable environments across orgs
takeaway: Users can create an environment once and reuse it in any org where they have repo access (enterprise opt-in).

title: Share with user groups
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. Settings has a User groups page where you create groups and add members. Wherever Manage access is available (secrets, environments, sessions, automations, plugins, playbooks, skills, MCP servers, knowledge), you can pick a user group as well as individual people or the org.
headline: Share Devin resources with user groups
takeaway: Admins can create user groups in Settings and share secrets, environments, sessions, and automations with them (enterprise opt-in).

title: Per-session sharing
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. Each session has its own sharing setting: just you, one or more user groups, your org or account-wide. Sessions that use a repo, secret or environment shared only with you or your group start as just you, with a warning before you widen it. Admins can set the org default.
headline: Per-session sharing controls
takeaway: Each session can be scoped to just you, user groups, your org, or account-wide, with warnings before widening private resources.

title: Slack session sharing change
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. Sessions started from Slack still reply in the channel, but only people the session is shared with can give it instructions. When someone else replies, Devin offers a one-click way to share the session with them.
headline: Devin restricts Slack session instructions to shared users
takeaway: Enterprise opt-in: Devin still replies in Slack channels, but only shared users can instruct it, with one-click sharing for others.

title: Granularly shareable secrets
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. When adding or editing a secret in an org, you can share it with a user group. By default it is shared with the org, as today.
headline: Devin adds user-group sharing for org secrets
takeaway: Enterprise opt-in: you can now scope secrets to specific user groups instead of the entire org, while keeping org-wide sharing as default.

title: Plugins, playbooks, skills, MCP servers and knowledge
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. Each can be shared with a user group instead of the whole org, including MCP servers that do not use OAuth.
headline: Devin supports user-group sharing for plugins, MCP servers, and knowledge
takeaway: Enterprise opt-in: share playbooks, skills, knowledge, and non-OAuth MCP servers with specific user groups instead of the whole org.

title: Automations
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. Automations also receive more granular permissions and can be shared with a user group. Sessions they start use the same sharing.
headline: Devin adds user-group permissions for automations
takeaway: Enterprise opt-in: share automations with specific user groups, and any sessions they start inherit those same sharing permissions.

title: Service users and bots
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. Service users and shared bots use only the repos and resources explicitly given to them; repo sync does not apply.
headline: Devin scopes service users and bots to explicit resources
takeaway: Enterprise opt-in: service users and shared bots only access explicitly granted repos and resources, without automatic repo sync.

title: Review shows only your repos
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. In an org, Review lists only repos and PRs you can access, including SCM mirrored access.
headline: Devin Review filters repos and PRs by user access
takeaway: Enterprise opt-in: Review only lists repos and PRs you can access, including SCM mirrored access.

title: DeepWiki and Ask use your repos
body: The access changes below are rolling out gradually and are off by default. Contact your Cognition representative to enable them for your enterprise. DeepWiki and Ask answer from the repos you can access, including SCM mirrored access.
headline: Devin DeepWiki and Ask scope answers to your accessible repos
takeaway: Enterprise opt-in: DeepWiki and Ask only answer using repos you can access, including SCM mirrored access.

title: Paste videos into session chat
body: Paste a video into the session chat composer to attach it, the same way you paste images.
headline: Devin lets you paste videos directly into session chat
takeaway: You can now paste videos into the session chat composer to attach them, just like pasting images.

title: More search options in the session IDE
body: The IDE's Search view adds match case, whole word and regex options, replace and replace all, and files to include or exclude.
headline: Session IDE search adds regex, replace, and file filters
takeaway: You can now use match case, whole word, regex, replace/replace all, and include/exclude file filters directly in the session IDE's Search view.

title: Citations open at the cited lines
body: Clicking a citation in Devin's message opens the file on the exact lines it cites.
headline: Message citations jump directly to cited file lines
takeaway: Clicking a citation in Devin's message opens the referenced file right at the exact lines cited, making code review faster.

title: Typo-tolerant settings search
body: Settings search and the command palette now find results even when a letter is missing.
headline: Settings search and command palette tolerate typos
takeaway: Settings search and the command palette still return matching results even if you miss a letter while typing.

title: Recent repositories first in repo pickers
body: The composer's repository picker and the @-mention repository list show your recently used repositories first.
headline: Repo pickers sort recently used repositories first
takeaway: Both the composer's repository picker and the @-mention repository list now surface your recently used repos at the top.

title: Triaged state for findings
body: Security findings gain a Triaged state and tab, for findings someone has looked at but not resolved yet.
headline: Security findings add a Triaged state and tab
takeaway: You can mark security findings as Triaged to track issues that have been reviewed but aren't resolved yet.

title: Summary cards and reviewer counts on PR reviews
body: Security > PR reviews adds summary cards and a Findings filter, and the reviewers card shows how many findings each reviewer found, fixed and dismissed.
headline: PR reviews add summary cards, filters, and reviewer counts
takeaway: Security > PR reviews now includes summary cards, a Findings filter, and counts of findings each reviewer found, fixed, and dismissed.

title: Set a finding's assignee through the API and MCP
body: A new API endpoint and MCP tool set or clear the assignee of a code scan finding.
headline: Assign or clear code scan findings via API and MCP
takeaway: A new API endpoint and MCP tool let you programmatically set or clear the assignee on a code scan finding.

title: Disable a plugin at a scope
body: In Settings > Customize, admins can disable a plugin for their organization or enterprise without uninstalling it.
headline: Admins can disable plugins at org or enterprise scope
takeaway: In Settings > Customize, admins can turn off a plugin for an organization or enterprise without uninstalling it.

title: Convert a shared outpost pool without draining it
body: Converting a shared outpost pool to account-wide no longer requires draining its organizations first.
headline: Convert shared outpost pools without draining
takeaway: You can switch a shared outpost pool to account-wide immediately without having to drain its organizations first.

title: Sazabi plugin
body: The Sazabi plugin is now in the plugin marketplace.
headline: Sazabi plugin added to Devin marketplace
takeaway: You can now install and use the Sazabi plugin directly from Devin's plugin marketplace.

title: Several installations of an API-key plugin MCP
body: An API-key plugin MCP can have another installation at personal, organization or enterprise scope.
headline: Multiple scopes for API-key plugin MCPs
takeaway: You can now install an API-key plugin MCP multiple times across personal, organization, or enterprise scopes.

title: Skills in the v3 Sessions API
body: The v3 Sessions API returns the skills each session used.
headline: v3 Sessions API now returns skills used
takeaway: When querying the v3 Sessions API, you can now see which skills each Devin session used.

title: Slack sender shown on watched thread replies
body: Replies in a watched Slack thread show in the session transcript under the sender's Slack name.
headline: Slack sender names shown in watched threads
takeaway: Replies from watched Slack threads now appear in your session transcript attributed to the sender's Slack name.

title: Introducing Devin Bots
body: Devin Bots are always-on Devins with their own identity, memory and permissions. Give a Bot a goal and it keeps doing the job: it breaks the work down, runs Devin sessions in parallel, each on its own cloud machine, and keeps each one going until the pull request is ready to merge. You set the direction and steer when it matters. Message your Bots in the web app or on Slack, text or call them, or add them to a group chat. Start from a template, such as a QA engineer, code reviewer or on-call engineer, or describe the outcome you want.
headline: Devin Bots launch as always-on autonomous Devins
takeaway: Assign goals to always-on Devin Bots that run parallel sessions until PRs are ready, and message or call them via web, Slack, or group chat.

title: Share Ask threads from the sidebar on mobile
body: On mobile, Ask thread rows in the sidebar now have a Share action that opens the device share sheet.
headline: Share Ask threads from mobile sidebar
takeaway: You can now share Ask threads directly from the mobile sidebar using your device's native share sheet.

title: Copy link for Ask threads in the sidebar
body: Ask thread rows in the sidebar now have a Copy link action.
headline: Copy links to Ask threads from the sidebar
takeaway: Grab a direct link to any Ask thread right from the sidebar to share or reference it quickly.

title: Typing outside a text box no longer enters the composer
body: Characters typed while no input is focused, such as after clicking in the transcript, are no longer inserted into the session or new-session composer; click the composer to type.
headline: Typing outside inputs no longer hits the composer
takeaway: Clicking the transcript and typing won't accidentally enter text into the composer; click the composer first.

title: Session header shows "Syncing" while a session catches up
body: When you open a session, its header shows an animated "Syncing" label next to the title until the session has caught up with the server.
headline: Session header shows Syncing status while catching up
takeaway: An animated Syncing label in the header lets you know when an opened session is still catching up with the server.

title: Plugin edits show as a plugin card in sessions
body: When Devin edits a plugin without needing an approval card (a pre-approved personal plugin or a Security plugin), the session transcript now shows the saved plugin card with what the edit changed and a link to the plugin.
headline: Pre-approved plugin edits now show a card in sessions
takeaway: When Devin edits a pre-approved personal or Security plugin, the transcript displays a saved card with changes and a link.

title: Quote attachments in chat from their tab
body: Attachment tabs in a session now have a "Quote in chat" button that adds the document to your message, and inline attachment cards keep a single Copy menu.
headline: Quote attachments in chat directly from their tab
takeaway: Use the Quote in chat button on attachment tabs to add documents to your message, with a single Copy menu on inline cards.

title: Artifact publishing names who will see it
body: Before you publish an artifact, the share dialog now says that anyone in your organization (named) will be able to view the page, and shows a warning when the session itself is private.
headline: Artifact share dialog names who can view it
takeaway: Before publishing, the dialog now names your organization as viewers and warns you if the underlying session is private.

title: Charge a repository's Reviews to an organization or budget
body: Repository billing rules in Review settings (Billing tab) let admins pick a repository and charge its Reviews, including Review chat, to an organization or budget instead of the PR author, manual launch or grant; organization Review managers can set rules for the repositories they manage.
headline: Charge repository Reviews to an organization or budget
takeaway: Admins and Review managers can set billing rules to charge a repo's Reviews and Review chat to an org or budget instead of the author.

title: Turn the Review list reading pane on or off
body: The Review list's reading pane beside the PR list can now be switched off, so clicking a row opens the pull request's full page instead; the choice is saved per account.
headline: Toggle Review list reading pane on or off
takeaway: You can now switch off the reading pane beside the PR list so clicking a row opens the full PR page; your preference is saved per account.

title: Show a stacked PR's merge target as its branch name
body: In Devin Review, the merge-target chip for a stacked PR can be switched between showing the target PR and its branch name, and the choice is remembered.
headline: Display stacked PR merge target as branch name
takeaway: In Devin Review, you can switch a stacked PR's merge-target chip between the target PR and its branch name, and the setting is remembered.

title: Before image shown for renamed image files
body: Devin Review's diff viewer now shows the Before image for image files a PR renames.
headline: Show Before image for renamed image files in diffs
takeaway: Devin Review's diff viewer now displays the original Before image when a pull request renames an image file.

title: Security sidebar groups less-used pages under More
body: The Security sidebar now moves less-used pages into a More menu, and you can pin a page to the sidebar or unpin it.
headline: Security sidebar groups less-used pages under More
takeaway: Less-used Security pages now live in a More menu, and you can pin or unpin any page to customize your sidebar.

title: Findings gains a By repository tab
body: On the Security Findings page, a new By repository tab lists each repository with its open findings count and last scan time, replacing the separate Security > Repositories page.
headline: Security Findings adds a By repository tab
takeaway: A new By repository tab on Security Findings shows each repo's open findings count and last scan time, replacing the separate Repositories page.

title: Link code-scan findings to an existing session via API
body: The v3 API and the devin_code_scan_manage MCP tool can now link one or more code-scan findings to an existing Devin session you own.
headline: Link code-scan findings to an existing session via API
takeaway: Use the v3 API or devin_code_scan_manage MCP tool to attach one or more code-scan findings directly to an existing Devin session you own.

title: Validation screenshots shown inline on findings
body: On a Security finding's detail page, image artifacts from the finding's validation are now shown inline instead of only as file links.
headline: Show validation screenshots inline on Security findings
takeaway: Image artifacts from a finding's validation now render inline on its detail page instead of appearing only as file links.

title: Choose base branch and PR grouping in Fix with Devin
body: Fix with Devin on code scan findings now always opens a dialog where you can set a base branch (default: repository default) and, for 2+ security-scan findings, choose one PR per root cause, one per finding, or one for all findings.
headline: Choose base branch and PR grouping in Fix with Devin
takeaway: Fix with Devin now opens a dialog to pick a base branch and, for 2+ findings, group fixes into one PR per root cause, per finding, or all together.

title: See running and failed validations on code scan findings
body: The code scan finding detail sheet now shows when a finding's validation is running ("Validating") or failed without a result ("Validation failed"), with a link to the validation session and the previous result.
headline: Code scan findings show running and failed validations
takeaway: You can now track validation status directly in the finding detail sheet, with links to the validation session and previous result.

title: Validate with Devin from a finding's detail view
body: The finding detail action bar in Security scans now has a Validate with Devin button for findings that can be validated.
headline: Validate with Devin button added to Security scan findings
takeaway: You can trigger Devin to validate eligible security scan findings directly from the finding detail action bar.

title: MCPs list redesigned with an Installed group and search
body: In Settings > Customize > MCPs, the MCP catalog now uses plugin-style rows, groups your installed MCPs under Installed above Available, and moves search into the header.
headline: MCPs list redesigned with Installed group and header search
takeaway: In Settings > Customize > MCPs, installed MCPs now appear above available ones with plugin-style rows and header search.

title: Confirm before discarding unsaved MCP setup changes
body: MCP setup sheets and editors (including enterprise MCP server settings) now ask for confirmation before closing or navigating away would discard unsaved input.
headline: Confirmation prompt before discarding unsaved MCP setup changes
takeaway: Prevents accidentally losing unsaved input when closing or navigating away from MCP setup sheets and enterprise server settings.

title: Customize shows organization- or enterprise-level installs
body: In Settings > Customize, plugins and MCPs that come from your organization or enterprise now say which level they are installed at.
headline: Customize shows org- or enterprise-level install badges
takeaway: In Settings > Customize, you can now see whether plugins and MCPs were installed at the organization or enterprise level.

title: MCP approval cards say what Always allow covers
body: The MCP tool approval card in sessions now names the tool and whether Always allow applies to all your sessions or everyone in the organization, and the resolved row shows Always allowed with a Change link.
headline: MCP approval cards clarify Always allow scope
takeaway: Approval cards now name the tool and show if Always allow applies to your sessions or the whole org, with a Change link afterward.

title: Plugin sheet notes MCPs you already installed separately
body: A plugin's sheet now tells you when its MCP is already installed on its own, explains that installing the plugin keeps it, and links to View MCP.
headline: Plugin sheet flags separately installed MCPs
takeaway: If a plugin's MCP is already installed, the plugin sheet notes that installing the plugin keeps it and provides a View MCP link.

body: Devin Review distinguishes a newly pushed commit from an existing commit that is ready to view and from analysis updates that leave the code unchanged. title: Voice Chat with Agents
body:
You can now talk with your agents in a realtime voice call. Describe a change out loud, ask what an agent is working on, and hear updates as the work moves forward.
Voice chat works in the Agents Window, the IDE, on web, and in Cursor for iOS.
Start a call
When the agent is idle and the chat input is empty, click the waveform button labeled **Start voice chat**. It sits where Send usually is, next to the microphone button for dictation.
On iOS, you can also say "Hey Siri, call Cursor" to start a call with a new agent, and mute or hang up from the Lock Screen with a Live Activity.
Talk while the agent works
The voice agent listens, replies, and hands coding work to the agent in your chat. While that agent runs, you can keep the conversation going. Ask what changed in a diff, check on a run, search earlier messages and calls with this agent, or switch between workers in a Project that has them.
The coding agent speaks for itself too. It shares short progress notes while it works and a brief answer when it's done, so you usually hear a short update instead of the full written reply.
Powered by Grok Voice
Voice chat runs on Grok Voice. Pick from many voices in Voice settings, including Ara, Eve, Leo, Rex, and Sal. With Privacy Mode on, voice chat runs with zero data retention.
Voice chat and dictation

takeaway: You can now talk with your agents in a realtime voice call. Describe a change out loud, ask what an agent is working on, and hear updates as the work moves forward.
